sections.html:
Benton County fills the far northwest corner of Arkansas, on the Springfield Plateau of the Ozarks, with Missouri to the north and Oklahoma to the west. Bentonville is the county seat and Rogers is the largest city. Other communities include Bella Vista, Bethel Heights, Cave Springs, Centerton, Decatur, Gentry, Gravette, Little Flock, Lowell, Pea Ridge, Siloam Springs and Sulphur Springs. Springdale and Elm Springs lie mostly in Washington County, though parts reach into Benton.

Walmart, headquartered in Bentonville, is the largest single influence, and growth has followed the jobs: 153,406 in 2000, 221,339 in 2010 and 284,333 in 2020. The 2025 estimate is 332,554. The median age is 35.3, and about 76 percent of residents live in urban areas. Median household income is the highest in the state.

Values rose 67.5 percent across the 2021 to 2024 reappraisal, slightly above what the assessor expected, driven by an imbalance between housing supply and demand. The next county-wide reappraisal is set for 2028.

The state assesses at 20 percent of appraised value, and yearly increases are held to 5 percent on a primary residence and 10 percent on commercial and industrial property. Because of caps and freezes, taxes do not rise at the pace of market value, so a buyer comparing two houses should ask what each one's capped value is and not just its appraisal.

sections.h2: Rules that change how a sale plays out
sections.html:
• After a sale, the property is assessed at 20 percent of its appraised value at the next assessment date after title transfers.
  • A buyer who receives title by sale cannot claim an assessment limitation until the second assessment date after the transfer. Amendment 79 caps the assessment on a principal residence once the owner is 65 or older, and it does not cap taxes.
  • The homestead credit is up to $600, covers the full bill if taxes are lower, and applies to a primary residence only, one credit per calendar year. The Homestead Department is at 479-271-1037.
  • The freeze applies to taxable value, not to taxes, so a higher millage rate can still raise the bill. Owners 65 or older, or on Social Security Disability, qualify.
  • Adding on to a home removes the freeze and reapplies it at the new value.

Home-based businesses are taxable, and business personal property tax is due October 15, paid one year behind.

sections.h2: Due dates and how to pay
sections.html:
Taxes are due by 11:59 p.m. on October 15. After that date a 10 percent late fee and or interest applies. The collector's calendar has tax books opening the first business day of March, May 31 as the deadline to assess, and July 1 as the last day to mail statements.

  • Online payment is open for current taxes, with a third-party fee of $3.99 for charges up to $110 and 3.59 percent above that.
  • Taxpayers with more than 50 parcels under one taxpayer ID cannot pay online, and payments post within 24 to 48 hours.
  • E-checks and phone payments have not been accepted since November 1, 2019.
  • A tax information request form for title companies is on the collector's site, which helps at closing.

Values come from the assessor. Disputes go to the county equalization board. Section 26-27-317 allows you to apply up to the third Monday in August, and you are owed written notice of the decision after the hearing.

An EF3 tornado 1.8 miles wide struck the county on May 26, 2024. If your house was hit or repaired, a buyer will ask whether the work was finished before listing. Some owners choose to sell as-is instead of repairing, since a lender-backed buyer may require the work to be completed. A cash buyer can look at the house in its present condition.

With values up 67.5 percent in the last reappraisal, many owners have more equity than they expect, and buyers have seen the same numbers. Price from recent sales of similar houses, not from the assessed value, since the assessment is only a share of the appraisal. List with your tax receipt in hand so a buyer can see exactly what the yearly bill has been, and be ready to explain whether caps or a freeze applied to your parcel.

If you are close to the October 15 deadline when you list, pay the current bill first. An open balance at the title stage slows everything down and gives a buyer a reason to ask for a credit.

The county sits on karst, so springs, sinkholes and caves are part of the ground under many lots. Houses near protected land, such as Pea Ridge National Military Park or Hobbs State Park-Conservation Area, or along Beaver Lake, can have lot shapes, slopes and access roads that differ from a flat subdivision lot. Ask an inspector about drainage and the foundation on such a property before you list.

sections.h2: Step by step: listing to closing
sections.html:
Begin with the tax record: look up your parcel, print the receipts and note the last appraised value. Then choose how to sell, with an agent or through a direct cash offer. When an offer is accepted, the title company opens a file and sends the tax information request form to the collector. The collector's answer shows what is owed for the current year and any earlier years. At closing you sign the deed, the county is paid from your proceeds, and you receive what remains.

Cash buyers remove the lender from the middle, so there is no appraisal wait and no repair list from a loan underwriter. That is especially useful for a storm-repaired house or a rental with deferred upkeep.

Pull the deed, your last tax receipt, any equalization board notice and records of repairs or additions. If you added on to the home, say so, since an addition removes the freeze and reapplies it at the new value, and a buyer may ask. Homestead credit holders should tell the buyer that the credit does not carry over. Heirs should have the death certificate and court papers ready, and landlords should bring leases and a list of any damage claims.

Taxes owed can be paid at closing. Ask the collector for the balance, use the title information request form on the collector's site, and give the figure to the closing agent. A sale also restarts the assessment clock for a new owner, so a seller in Bentonville, Rogers or Bella Vista should know the house's last appraised value and when the next county-wide reappraisal is due.

Few sellers think about getting around, yet buyers from out of state do. US 62 and US 71 run through the county, and Northwest Arkansas National Airport (XNA) is near Highfill, which helps out-of-town buyers.

faqs.q: When is the Benton County property tax deadline?
faqs.a: October 15 at 11:59 p.m. After that, a 10 percent late fee and or interest applies.

faqs.q: Who handles property tax appeals in Benton County?
faqs.a: The assessor sets value and the county equalization board hears appeals. An owner may apply to the board on or before the third Monday in August.

faqs.q: Does the homestead credit transfer to a buyer?
faqs.a: No. The credit is for a primary residence, one per calendar year, and a buyer must apply on their own. A buyer who gets title by sale cannot claim an assessment limitation until the second assessment date after the transfer.

faqs.q: How can I get a tax figure for a closing?
faqs.a: The collector's website has a tax information request form for title companies, along with a tax record search where you can print receipts.

faqs.q: Is there a fee to pay Benton County taxes by card?
faqs.a: Yes. The online vendor charges $3.99 for payments of $110 or less and 3.59 percent above $110.
